title: Every second teaches or protects a fact
statement: Cut anything in a teaching video that cannot name the fact it teaches or protects.
example: The rule's companion file puts the cost of interesting but irrelevant details at an effect size of about −0.37 to −0.41.
detail: The science video agent's spec sets a single objective: every second must encode a target fact or protect the encoding of one, a second that does neither is a cut candidate, and completion is not success (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g7-science/brainlifts/video-generation-agent-v0.2.md`). Its rule 3 cuts any element that cannot name its target fact and turns off music under narration, decorative b-roll, textured backgrounds, non-process motion and off-topic jokes by default. The companion file gives the reason: interesting but irrelevant material tends to depress learning, about g −0.37 to −0.41 for seductive details, and its sources include a 2012 meta-analysis of the seductive-detail effect (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g7-science/brainlifts/video-generation-human-v0.2.md`). Keep music and sound effects out from under the teaching voice unless a sound has an instructional job, and leave decorative footage and textured backgrounds off by default.
against: It is a default, not a ban: an element stays when the storyboard names the instructional job it does, and the companion file says to revisit the rule if the project's own delayed-recall data disagree (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g7-science/brainlifts/video-generation-human-v0.2.md`). The 20 dB gap is listed as an operating heuristic still to be tested against recall and intelligibility, and the evidence corpus behind these rules skews adult and higher-ed, with elementary effects non-significant (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g7-science/brainlifts/video-generation-human-v0.2.md`). A later run found: A unit's opening film was required to carry an atmospheric, theatrical intro sound following the script, then background music, with the target an atmospheric score under the narration, swells timed to the story and the words clear throughout. The score was never mixed with narration and nothing measured its effect (`g9/transcript/chat-transcript.redacted.txt`).
